chapter.heading: The Greatest Gift
chapter.v:
Though I
speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal. [1 Cor. 3:9]

And though
I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing. [Is. 49:8 #]

And though
I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profits me nothing. [Rom. 14:13]

does not
rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth;

bears all
things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. [2 Cor. 7:14]

Love never
fails. But whether there are prophecies, they will fail; whether there are tongues, they will cease; whether there is knowledge, it will vanish away.

For we
know in part and we prophesy in part. [2 Cor. 4:2; 5:11]

But when
that which is perfect has come, then that which is in part will be done away. [1 Cor. 1:5;]

When I
was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child; but when I became a man, I put away childish things. [Is. 60:5; 2 Cor.]

For now
we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I shall know just as I also am known. [2 Cor. 12:15]

And now
abide faith, hope, love, these three; but the greatest of these is love. [1 Cor. 4:14]
